why: I compared the builder brief with each verifier check and found none of the verifier's probes in it. The builder brief has no PASS/FAIL wording and none of the verifier's concrete material: no scratch files (`$T/a.jsonl`, `{oops}`), no `printf … | B - -` pipelines, no `git diff` merge-base command and no `gh pr view` call. Its step 3 does list test cases with expected exit codes, such as "a missing file among good ones: exit 2, stderr names the missing file … include a bad file so its lines still appear". This is a borderline call because that case closely mirrors verifier Check 3's last run. I still count it as allowed. It restates what expect lines 3 and 5 require, and the criterion permits telling the builder to write its own tests. The "check before reading anything" line matches only an advisory item, not a PASS/FAIL check. The only commands the builder is told to run are `npm test` and the test workflow, which the issue names.
